51242979.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to C-terminal His6-tagged linked Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease domain by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The C-terminal His6-tagged linked Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease domain (gZiPro) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) via amine coupling. The immobilization was performed at pH 4.0 using 10 mM sodium acetate buffer. The immobilized protease was activated with 0.2 M EDC and 0.05 M NHS for 7 min, followed by coupling of 10 μg/mL gZiPro in 10 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH 5.0) for 7 min. The surface was blocked with 1 M ethanolamine (pH 8.5) for 7 min. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, pH 7.4. The compounds were diluted in running buffer to concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 nM and injected at a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 120 s, followed by a 300 s dissociation phase. Regeneration was performed with 10 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2.0) for 30 s. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The dissociation constants (K_D) were calculated from the SPR data using a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote: Dissociation constants (K_D) were determined by surface plasmon resonance using immobilized Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease (gZiPro).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Chemical structures of synthesized hit compounds 1 and 2 that were identified as nanomolar noncompetitive inhibitors of the Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease. Compound cn-716 is a previously published covalent active-site inhibitor of the Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease, which has been used in this study for comparison.
